questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.**

ENTHRALL
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'enchant.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given word 'Enthrall' means **to fill someone with overwhelming emotion as wonder or delight**. (मंत्रमुग्‍ध कर देना, मोहित करना)

 
 
• Example: *During intervals, the locals **enthrall** the audiences with traditional and cultural performances*.
 
 
 
• ​Let's see the meaning of the given options:-
 
 
• 'Eject' means **to push or send somebody or something out of a place usually with force**. (किसी व्‍यक्ति या वस्‍तु को प्रायः ज़बरदस्‍ती निकाल बाहर करना)
 
 
• Example: *The pilot managed to **eject** from the jet without sustaining injuries*.
 
 
 
• 'Enchant' means **to fill someone with great delight; charm**. (मंत्रमुग्‍ध कर देना, प्रसन्न करना)
 
 
• Example: *She has endless stories that **enchant **and inform the kids*.
 
 
 
• 'Repel' means **to make somebody feel disgusted**. (वितृष्‍ण या घृणा पैदा कर देना)
 
 
• Example: *I was **repelled** by the smell*.
 
 
 
• 'Incite' means **to encourage somebody to do something by making him or her very angry or excited**. (भड़काना, उकसाना)
 
 
• Example: *She doesn't want to **incite** any kind of violence*.

 
 
 
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The synonyms of the word 'Enthrall' are "**enchant, fascinate, mesmerize**".
 
• The antonyms of the word 'Enthrall' are "**bore, tire, weary**".

questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment In the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

He said he had being playing tennis since he was eight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**he had being**' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the verb 'being' is incorrect.
 
• The given sentence is in the **past perfect continuous** tense as it is talking about **an ongoing action that started and continued for some time in the past**.
 
• Also, to indicate **time reference** ''**for**'' and ''**since**'' are used in the past perfect continuous tense and it describes **when the action started and how long it continued in the past**.
 
• The past perfect continuous tense is constructed using **had + been + the verb’s present participle **(here, **playing**).

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *He said **he had been** playing tennis since he was eight*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• दिए गए वाक्य में verb 'being' का प्रयोग गलत है।
 
• दिया गया वाक्य **past perfect continuous tense** में है क्योंकि **यह एक चल रही क्रिया के बारे में बात कर रहा है जो अतीत में कुछ समय के लिए शुरू हुई और जारी रही**।
 
• इसके अलावा, समय के संदर्भ को इंगित करने के लिए ''**for**'' और ''**since**'' का उपयोग **past perfect continuous tense** में किया जाता है और यह वर्णन करता है कि **कार्रवाई कब शुरू हुई और कितनी देर तक यह अतीत में जारी रही**।
 
• **Past perfect continuous tense** का निर्माण: had + been + the verb’s present participle (यहाँ, playing) का उपयोग करके किया गया है।

 

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 है।

सही वाक्य: *He said he had been playing tennis since he was eight*.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate word to fill In the blank.**

He met _______ an accident a few years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'with.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is talking about **an accident that happened a few years ago**.
 
• **Meet with something** is a** phrasal verb** that means **to experience something, usually something unpleasant**.
 
• For Examples:-
 
 
• I heard she'd **met with an accident.**
 
• If you **meet with any difficulties**, just let me know.

 
 
 

Conclusion: About someone who met with an accident a few years ago.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Complete Sentence: *He met **with** an accident a few years ago*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• दिया गया वाक्य **कुछ साल पहले हुए एक हादसे की बात** कर रहा है।
 
• Meet with something एक वाक्यांश क्रिया है जिसका अर्थ है** कुछ अनुभव करना, आमतौर पर कुछ अप्रिय।**
 
• उदाहरण के लिए:-
 
 
• I heard she'd **met with an accident.**

 If you **meet with any difficulties**, just let me know.
 
 

Conclusion: किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति के बारे में जो कुछ साल पहले दुर्घटना का शिकार हुआ हो।

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

पुरा वाक्य: *He met with an accident a few years ago*.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

I went to the market __buying few__ vegetables and milk.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**to buy some**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the underlined segment, the use of the gerund 'buying' and the **determiner 'few'** is incorrect.
 
• A **gerund** is a **verb form that functions as a noun **and is** not required **as per the context of the sentence.
 
• The **to-infinitive** should be used **in place of** the **gerund 'buying'**.
 
• The to-infinitive is used in many sentence constructions, often expressing the purpose of something or someone's opinion about something.
 
• The to-infinitive is formed as to + base form of the verb (here, buy).
 
• Also, in the given sentence, the **noun 'milk' **is an **uncountable noun**.
 
• The **determiner ''few''** is applied to countable objects while the **determiner ''some''** is applicable to **both countable and uncountable objects**.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct Sentence: *I went to the market **to buy some** vegetables and milk*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• रेखांकित खंड में, gerund 'buying' और determiner 'few' का उपयोग गलत है।
 
• Gerund एक क्रिया रूप है जो संज्ञा के रूप में कार्य करता है और वाक्य के संदर्भ के अनुसार इसकी आवश्यकता नहीं है।
 
• Gerund 'buying' के स्थान पर to-infinitive का उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• To-infinitive का उपयोग कई वाक्य निर्माणों में किया जाता है, जो अक्सर **किसी चीज़ के उद्देश्य या किसी चीज़ के बारे में किसी की राय व्यक्त करते हैं**।
 
• To-infinitive: to + base form of the verb (यहाँ, buy) के रूप में बनता है।
 
• साथ ही दिए गए वाक्य में **'milk' संज्ञा** एक uncountable** संज्ञा **है।
 
• Determiner ''few'' countable objects पर लागू होता है जबकि determiner ''some'' countable और uncountable वस्तुओं दोनों पर लागू होता है।

 

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

सही वाक्य: *I went to the market to buy some vegetables and milk*.

__
 
• The given word 'Cherish' means **to love somebody or something and look after him or her or it carefully**. (किसी से स्‍नेह करना और सावधानीपूर्वक देखरेख में रखना)

• Example: *The relief agency will **distribute** the food among several countries*.
 
 
 
• 'Disperse' means **to separate and go in different directions; to make somebody or something do this**. (बिखर जाना, विसर्जित हो जाना; बिखरा देना, विसर्जित कर देना)

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required.’**

The pilgrims __were fined them__ one thousand rupees each for littering around the shrine.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**were fined**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the underlined segment, the use of the pronoun 'them' is superfluous or not required.
 
• The given sentence is talking about the pilgrims who were fined for littering around the shrine.
 
• A **sentence** follows **Subject** (**The pilgrims**) **+ Verb** (**were fined**) **+ Object** (**one thousand rupees each for littering around the shrine**) word order.
 
• The **subject-verb agreement** of the **plural subject ''The pilgrims''** with the **plural verb 'were'** is correct.
 
• Therefore, the pronoun 'them' **should be removed** from the sentence.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *The pilgrims **were fined** one thousand rupees each for littering around the shrine.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• रेखांकित खण्ड में pronoun 'them' का प्रयोग **फालतू है या आवश्यक नहीं है**।
 
• दिया गया वाक्य **तीर्थयात्रियों को दी गई सजा के बारे में बात कर रही है, जिन पर मंदिर के आसपास कूड़ा डालने के लिए जुर्माना लगाया गया था**।
 
• एक वाक्य, Subject (The pilgrims) + Verb (were fined) + Object (one thousand rupees each for littering around the shrine) शब्द क्रम का अनुसरण करता है।
 
• Plural verb 'were' के साथ plural subject ''The pilgrims'' का subject-verb agreement सही है।
 
• इसलिए वाक्य से pronoun 'them' हटा देना चाहिए।

 

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

सही वाक्य: *The pilgrims **were fined** one thousand rupees each for littering around the shrine.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.** 

Why are you __stood__ here at this late hour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'standing.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the underlined segment, the use of the past tense form of the verb 'stood' is incorrect.
 
• The simple past tense is used **to talk about things that happened or existed before now**.
 
 
• The **formula for asking a question** in the **simple past tense** is: **did + subject + root form of the verb**.
 
 
 
• The given sentence is **asking someone why he/she is standing here when it's so late**.
 
• We use the present continuous tense when an action or condition is happening now, frequently, and may continue into the future.
 
 
• The present continuous formula: **auxiliary verb (am, is, are) + subject + the present participle form of the verb **(here, **standing**) **+ object**.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the present participle form of the verb 'standing' should be used in place of the past tense form of the verb 'stood'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *Why are you **standing** here at this late hour?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• रेखांकित खण्ड में verb 'stood' का प्रयोग **गलत है**।
 
• Simple past tense का इस्तेमाल **उन चीजों के बारे में बात करने के लिए किया जाता है जो अब से पहले हुई या मौजूद थीं**।

• The given sentence "***Hormones, which are ___(5)___ growth chemicals, help the body to repair itself and grow***.'' is indicating hormones are important to help the body to repair itself and grow.
 
• The use of the word ''help'' in the sentence indicates **to make something better or easier**.
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'special'.
 
• The word 'special' means important for som
